title: Blueberry Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Mostly-milk custard with cooked blueberries stirred in before churning; cream added for body.
summary: Our classic French custard made with mostly milk for a lighter base, then mixed with jammy cooked blueberries before churning. Fruity, purple-streaked and not too rich.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the berries
steps.text: Cook the blueberries and 80 g sugar in the small saucepan over medium-low heat for about 12 min, until the berries burst and the juice thickens. Cool and chill.

steps.title: Warm the dairy
steps.text: Heat the milk and cream with the 110 g sugar until steaming.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk the yolks and salt, then whisk in a little hot dairy before adding the rest and pouring it back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook gently
steps.text: Stir slowly over the lowest heat until the custard is 77-80 °C and silky. Rushing it over high heat makes it curdle.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain, stir in the vanilla, cool in the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Stir in the cold blueberries and their juice, churn and freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Frozen wild blueberries give the most intense colour.
A common mistake is adding warm berries to the custard, which can make the churned ice cream icy.
Stir the berries in only briefly if you prefer purple ripples rather than an all-lilac ice cream.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks.
